paragraphs.title: The Siege of Jerusalem and the Disappearance of Its Enemies

easy.explanation: Jerusalem is called Ariel in verse 1.
easy.q: What is Jerusalem called at the beginning of the passage?

answers: It will experience distress and sorrow
It will become a fruitful field
easy.explanation: The Lord says that Ariel will be distressed and filled with heaviness and sorrow.

answers: As a dream of a night vision
easy.explanation: The multitude of nations fighting against Ariel will be like a dream of a night vision.
easy.q: How are the enemies of Jerusalem eventually described?

medium.explanation: Like a dream that disappears upon waking, the enemies' expected victory will not last.
medium.q: What does the comparison to a dream of a night vision suggest about Jerusalem's enemies?

medium.explanation: In this context, "munition" refers to Jerusalem's defensive works or fortifications.
medium.q: What does the word "munition" mean in the phrase "her munition"?

medium.explanation: The dream ends when the hungry man awakens, and his soul is still empty; so it will be with the attacking nations.
medium.q: What happens to the nations' imagined victory, like the hungry man's dream of eating?

challenge.explanation: Verse 6 says that Ariel will be visited by the Lord of hosts with thunder, earthquake, and great noise.
challenge.q: Who brings judgment upon the enemies of Ariel?

answers: Jerusalem suffers for a time, but its enemies' power disappears
Jerusalem disappears while its enemies grow stronger
Both Jerusalem and its enemies remain unchanged
challenge.explanation: Ariel undergoes distress and humiliation, while the nations fighting against it become like a vanishing dream.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears between Jerusalem and its enemies?

challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses that the change will happen suddenly and unexpectedly.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the phrase "at an instant suddenly"?

paragraphs.title: Spiritual Blindness and the Sealed Book

easy.explanation: They are described as drunken and staggering, though they have not been drinking wine.
easy.q: How are the people described spiritually?

easy.explanation: The Lord has poured out upon them the spirit of deep sleep.
easy.q: What has the Lord poured out upon the people?

easy.explanation: The learned man says that he cannot read it because it is sealed.
easy.q: What does the learned man say when he is given the sealed book?

answers: Spiritual dullness and inability to understand
medium.explanation: The image of deep sleep represents spiritual blindness and a lack of understanding.
medium.q: What does "deep sleep" represent in this passage?

answers: One is learned but cannot read the sealed book, while the other is not learned
Both can read the open book
Both refuse to read a book that is not sealed
medium.explanation: The learned man cannot read because the book is sealed, while the other says he is not learned.
medium.q: What is the difference between the two people who receive the book?

answers: Their hearts are far from the Lord, and their fear is taught by human commandment
They never speak about the Lord
They have no religious customs at all
medium.explanation: They honor the Lord with their mouths and lips, but their hearts are far from Him.
medium.q: Why is there a gap between the people's words and their hearts?

answers: They are unable to understand the meaning of what they see
challenge.explanation: The learned cannot read the sealed book, and the unlearned cannot read it either, illustrating spiritual inability to understand.
challenge.q: What does the sealed book illustrate about the people's condition?

answers: Their outward worship perfectly matches their hearts
The Lord exposes the difference between their words and their hearts
Their hidden actions are better than their speech
challenge.explanation: They honor the Lord outwardly while keeping their hearts far from Him and hiding their works in darkness.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the people's outward worship and their hidden actions?

answers: The wisdom of the wise will perish, and the understanding of the prudent will be hidden
The people will receive great riches
The enemies will build a new siege
challenge.explanation: The Lord declares that the wisdom of the wise will perish and the understanding of the prudent will be hid.
challenge.q: What result follows the description of the people's outward worship and hidden counsel?

answers: They will rejoice in the Lord
They will disappear from the land
easy.explanation: The meek will increase their joy in the Lord and rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

answers: The terrible one and the scorner
easy.explanation: The terrible one is brought to nothing, and the scorner is consumed.
easy.q: Who will be brought to nothing and consumed?

answers: The one who reproves in the gate and the just
easy.explanation: They lay a snare for the one who reproves in the gate and turn aside the just.
easy.q: Whom do the evildoers trap and turn aside?

medium.explanation: The terrible one represents a powerful and oppressive person.
medium.q: What does "the terrible one" refer to in this passage?

medium.explanation: Lebanon becoming a fruitful field and the fruitful field being counted as a forest picture a reversal of conditions.
medium.q: What change is described in the images of Lebanon and the fruitful field?

answers: Both are parts of the restoration of justice
The meek rejoice because they become oppressors
medium.explanation: The downfall of the oppressors makes room for the meek and poor to rejoice in the Lord.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the removal of oppressors and the joy of the meek?

answers: Oppressors are weakened, while the humble receive joy
The humble are weakened, while oppressors grow stronger
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the removal of the terrible and the scorner with the joy of the meek.
challenge.q: What is the main reversal in this passage?

answers: They trap or hinder the person who publicly corrects wrongdoing
They invite the reprover to a feast
They teach the reprover how to read
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes opposition against the person who speaks against wrongdoing in public.
challenge.q: What does it mean that evildoers "lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate"?

answers: The righteous are diverted from justice over a trivial matter
The righteous leave the land forever
challenge.explanation: The evildoers cause the just to be turned aside for something worthless or insignificant.
challenge.q: What does "turn aside the just for a thing of nought" reveal about justice?

paragraphs.title: The Restoration of the House of Jacob

answers: He will no longer be ashamed
easy.explanation: The Lord says that Jacob shall not now be ashamed.
easy.q: What will happen to Jacob in the future?

easy.explanation: When they see the work of the Lord, they will sanctify His name and fear the God of Israel.
easy.q: What will Jacob's children do when they see the work of the Lord?

easy.explanation: Those who have erred in spirit shall come to understanding.
easy.q: What will those who have erred in spirit eventually gain?

answers: Seeing the work of the Lord in their midst
The disappearance of the sealed book
medium.explanation: They will sanctify God's name when they see the work of His hands among them.
medium.q: What will lead Jacob's children to sanctify the Lord's name?

answers: Went astray in understanding or devotion
medium.explanation: It refers to people who have gone astray spiritually and need understanding.
medium.q: What does the phrase "erred in spirit" mean?

answers: By renewed reverence for God and increased understanding
medium.explanation: Restoration includes the sanctifying of God's name and the gaining of understanding and instruction.
medium.q: How is the restoration of the people described?

answers: Earlier worship is merely outward, but later worship comes with recognition and reverence
Earlier there is no speech, and later there are no actions
There is no change between the two sections
challenge.explanation: Earlier the people honor God with their lips while their hearts are far away; later they see His work and sanctify His name.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the earlier description of worship and the ending of the passage?

answers: Restoration includes inward change and the gaining of understanding
Restoration concerns only the rebuilding of houses
challenge.explanation: The restored community includes people who move from spiritual error and murmuring to understanding and instruction.
challenge.q: How is the restoration of Jacob connected with those who have gone astray?

answers: Restoration removes shame and renews the people's relationship with God
Restoration is only an outward political change
Restoration leads the people away from God
challenge.explanation: The passage joins renewed dignity for Jacob with genuine reverence for the Holy One of Jacob.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jacob no longer being ashamed and his children sanctifying God's name?
